findings.title: Heat loss at Window #1
findings.description: Heat loss detected at window visible in 3 images. Temperature readings range from 0.0°C to 0.0°C, averaging 0.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Install thermal curtains or cellular shades to reduce heat loss through glazing
Add weather stripping around window frame to eliminate drafts
Consider secondary glazing or low-E window film for improved insulation
Check for gaps around frame and seal with appropriate caulk or expanding foam
Inspect window hardware and ensure proper closure and lock engagement
recommendations.description: Windows are a major source of heat loss in buildings. Even modern double-glazed units can lose significant heat, while single-glazed windows are particularly problematic.

findings.title: Heat loss at Wall #3
findings.description: Heat loss detected at wall visible in 3 images. Temperature readings range from 0.0°C to 0.0°C, averaging 0.0°C. This represents moderate heat loss that should be addressed.

advice: Inspect cavity wall insulation levels and top up if necessary
Consider external wall insulation (EWI) for solid wall properties
Investigate internal wall insulation (IWI) as alternative to EWI
Check for thermal bridging at structural elements (lintels, columns)
Investigate any signs of damp or missing insulation in cavity
Consider thermal render or insulated plasterboard solutions
recommendations.description: Wall heat loss is one of the largest contributors to energy waste in buildings. Solid walls lose heat twice as fast as cavity walls, and poorly insulated cavity walls are also highly inefficient.
